Different retraction maps affect spherical residual stability mainly through how they turn update magnitude into a rotation angle on the hypersphere. On the sphere, the papers say all retractions reduce to this single scalar choice; some produce angles that saturate instead of growing without bound, and finite-p angular retractions gave the best validation loss, suggesting the exponential map is not the most stable or preferred choice for spherical residual streams [1]. In particular, projection- and Cayley-based spherical normalizations are exactly norm-preserving and use only algebraic operations, while the exponential map is just one endpoint in the same spectrum [1].

A related result also favors Cayley-style spherical/orthogonal updates for stability: an adaptive Cayley rotation preserves orthogonality for all inputs and achieved the best long-horizon stability among compared residual methods, with strong norm preservation [6]. However, that paper studies orthogonal residual connections more broadly rather than the specific one-parameter spherical retraction family analyzed in [1].
